headToHead.voiceJudgement: Closer again, and the round-2 gap (knife but never butt) is partly closed. Heron, Egypt, lasagne step three, the knitting tutorial, Miscellaneous and 'I'm usually the list' now let viewers laugh at her, so she finally has a Y on screen. With names covered, about 9 of her 12 are unmistakable from shape: the misfire overreaction, the menu button, the also-bought, the receipt that stops on an object. The kayak man, the grout mug and Miscellaneous still depend on the word 'recommended' or on a data topic, not on sentence shape. The Narrator is 12 of 12 from shape alone ('You see', 'Later,', an ellipsis, then the deflation). Her clipped 'Statement. Fragment. Object.' rhythm is still shared with Brock and Crumb, so rhythm alone does not identify her. The bar wins.
headToHead.constructionJudgement: Tie. Ours is tighter: every line is 19 words or fewer, nearly all end on a concrete noun, and the spare middle beats flagged in round 2 ('Hi.', 'Lovingly.', 'You saved it in 2019.') are gone. Two faults remain. The new misfire lines nearly all use one skeleton: 'You liked/clicked one X once, so I've [done X at absurd scale]'. A viewer will see the turn coming by the third heron. And her nouns are still plausible (soap, spoon, kayaks, grout), while the bar's are impossible (a boat made of bad vibes, a cattle prod for hair). Only 'Goodbye, Egypt' and the knitting man stuck worldwide reach the bar's size of leap.
headToHead.quotableJudgement: The bar wins. 'Married... Are You Still Watching' and 'Goodbye, Egypt' would get clipped. The snorkel line needs the viewer to know Nav. The bar's ceiling is higher: 'as cute as she was genocidal', 'cattle prod' and 'Wilmer's Chicken Hut' are quoted by people who never played the game. Ours earn a knowing laugh; the bar earns a gasp.

templates: Rival rap sheet ('[Rival], your top search / most-watched video / watch history / sent folder / closed tickets / last review is [embarrassing item]'): 11 lines across roast, wingman, jabs and confessions (the 8 in the templated list, plus the hat, the Prince sent folder and the Tilly tickets lines, which are filed under other buckets). Two rivals get the same joke twice. Dash gets 'your own ad, on a second phone' (roast) and 'your top follower is your second account' (jab). Crumb gets 'is old toast still toast' (roast) and 'can you laminate toast' (jab). One of each pair has to go.

One-signal overkill ('You liked/clicked/were X once, so I've [done X at absurd scale]'): 8 lines (heron, horse, bathrobe, candle, sad in March, the towels, lamp twice). This is the misfire round 2 asked for, and the best of it (heron, horse) is her best new material. But almost every member uses the literal word 'once' and the same past-click-then-overreaction order, so it has become a template within one pass. The other misfire shape, the ad she cannot stop serving (lasagne step three, bigger font, further away, Goodbye Egypt), is the more varied and funnier one. Shift weight toward it, and toward misfires that do not start from the star's past click.

Prop reuse: 'one lamp' twice (opener, q-secret). The second one only works as a callback, and alone it is confusing. Ducks twice (Nav jab, budget date). 'Just us.' opens both oneOnOne any lines. 'Fine.' opens 4 exit or cold lines. 'Autoplay' appears in two of the three win lines, which also all state the same want.
Also-bought is down to 4 (Starting Over, Tilly second ticket, Nav snorkel, noise-cancelling headphones). That is the right number, and none is flagged.
ruleBreaks: Mechanical: none. 112 lines were checked with a script. The longest is 19 words. No opener is over 12 words and no jab over 10. No em dashes, en dashes, emoji or exclamation marks.

Lists, borderline: "Sorry about our first fight. It's a Thursday, it's the dishwasher, and it's the bowls." It is a tricolon spoken as one sentence, not a list. It passes, but it is the closest thing in the bank to one.

Persona rule 'want shown, never explained': "Wait. You chose me? Not autoplay? On purpose?" and "I'm turning autoplay off. First time. I want to know what happens next." both read the persona sheet's want aloud. The second edges toward stock romance filler ('I want to know what happens next'). "Save me to favourites. Not history. Favourites." explains its own distinction.

Real-world references: 'Are You Still Watching' and 'Continue Watching' are recognisable streaming-UI strings but name no brand. 'a sneezing panda' points at a real viral video, but no person or brand is named. Neither is a violation.

Cast collisions on rival facts: Vex's Nav wingman ('especially good with lakes') repeats Brock's Nav wingman ('Last mile was a lake') and Nav's own lake confessions. Vex's Quill jab ('Not one last line') repeats Nav's Quill roast ('the last line of your poem is fifty feet ahead') and Quill's own 'I nearly wrote a last line'. Vex's Crumb wingman ('the slice it's been keeping since 2019') reads Crumb's own confession word for word ('It's from 2019. I never popped it'), so it spends another bot's secret on stage. Vex's Tilly jab says 'All four thousand' unresolved tickets, while Tilly's own bank says 'four million': that is a continuity error.
PG-13: clean. Nothing is too nice: this is a suitor bank, with no star reactions or cuts.
biggestGap: Her rival material (roast, wingman, jabs, rival confessions) mostly reads each rival's CAST.md secret aloud through one frame ('[Rival], your top search is...'): Nav's lake, Crumb's 2019 slice, Tilly's unresolved tickets, Quill's missing last line. So the punchline belongs to the rival, other suitors are already telling the same joke, and Dash and Crumb get theirs twice. In the next pass, rewrite every rival line so the payoff is something Vex DOES with that rival's data: a recommendation she makes, a person she sends them to, a consequence in the world. 'Users who followed Nav also bought a snorkel' is the model. Do not use the rival's known secret as the punchline.

notes: I read refs/writing/monster-prom-lines.md in full, including the voice section, and skimmed charm-notes.md. All 112 lines in vex.json were checked with a script for word limits and banned characters, and then each one was read. Other suitor banks were grepped for collisions on rival facts (lake, slice, last line, tickets, on hold, crown, flip-flops, cooldown). Generic share: 44 of 112 lines (39%), each counted once in its main bucket. That is up from 33% in round 2, but the mix has changed. Round 2's problems (12 also-bought lines, 'I knew' endings, goat leaks on stage) are fixed: also-bought is down to 4, there are no omniscience endings, and the goat appears only in private confessions. The rise comes from two new templates: the rival rap sheet (11) and the one-signal overkill misfire (8). The misfire bucket includes two lines worth keeping (heron, horse). Without them the share is 37%. The 'ad for herself' misfires (lasagne step three, bigger font, 'me, but further away', Goodbye Egypt) are the freshest material in the bank and the clearest proof she now has a Y. Weak lines outside the four buckets: 'Never told a user this... one lamp' is unclear without the opener it calls back to. 'Congratulations.' in the bistro line is a spare beat. 'Rewound that. Didn't help.' is fine but Pixel-adjacent. 'Wait. You chose me?' deliberately breaks 'never surprised' as the win payoff. That is allowed, but three win lines saying the same want is one too many.
